incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate and sustained GPU paging detected on runtime-prod-us-east (pool=model-runner-99). Start=2141597530

Jordan H.: Im here. whats the customer impact? @Priya

Priya K. (CS): two paying tenants reporting 504s and failed backfills starting ~2141597515. several support tickets created. one tenant saw ~120 failed requests. will compile a list for replay.

Mateo R. (runtime oncall): grabbing logs. quick summary so far: one host in model-runner-99 has repeating cudaMalloc failures and heavy kvcache eviction churn. looks like paging -> CPU fallback -> increased latency -> 5xx. pulling traces and nvidia snapshots now.

Mateo R.: tail logs (snip):
```
[2141597514] WARN runtime: cuda allocation failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2141597516] ERROR handler: generation aborted: OOM at step 192
[2141597518] INFO kvcache: evicting 2400 entries (evict_ratio=0.38) reason=prefix_miss
[2141597522] WARN runtime: fallback to host cpu path (slow)
```

Mateo R.: nvidia-smi sample:
```
GPU 0: 24GiB total, 23.9GiB used (peak 24GiB)
Processes: model_runner(pid=45902)
FB Memory Usage: 23.9/24 GiB
```

Priya K.: timeline note: traffic spike at 2141597490 after a client flipped on grouped-batching. batch-size>=10 fraction jumped from ~3% -> ~45% for ~6m. seq lengths: median 80, 95pct ~1400.

Aya N. (eng-ml): if kvcache is cold and batch sizes jump with long seqs, the cache will balloon and allocator pressure spikes. two likely contributors: raw working set > GPU RAM and fragmentation causing allocs to fail.

Jordan H.: immediate mitigation suggestions? can we do quick config changes to stop customer impact?

Lin S. (eng-sre): options and tradeoffs: 
- reduce pool max_batch to 5 (fast, limits throughput)
- disable kvcache on the offending host(s) temporarily (reduces mem but increases compute)
- spin an extra replica and redirect traffic away from hot host (takes minutes)
- request client to rollback grouped-batching (coordinate with product)

Mateo R.: applying max_batch throttle now: `redwoodctl pool update --id model-runner-99 --max-batch 5` -> OK on 5/5 hosts

incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: pool update applied to model-runner-99. Verifying health.

Mateo R.: monitoring. error rate dropped from ~18% -> ~5% within 90s. still seeing occasional OOM logs while queued fans drain.

Priya K.: customer comms: told affected tenants were mitigating and will follow up with replay guidance. will compile list of dropped request ids.

Mateo R.: performing controlled kvcache disable on host runner-99b to validate effect: `redwoodctl runtime set --host runner-99b --kvcache=false` -> applied.

Mateo R.: result: host runner-99b memory footprint decreased ~2.2GiB and no further cudaMalloc failures observed on that host for the last ~4m. other hosts still show occasional failures.

OpsBot: saved request traces to gs://redwood-incident-logs/2141597530/traces/ and requests list to gs://redwood-incident-logs/2141597530/requests.csv

Aya N.: repro plan: stress with long seqs and larger batches to try to reproduce fragmentation/alloc pattern. sharing script: 
```
# repro memory pressure
for B in 6 10 14; do
  python stress_repro.py --batch $B --seq 2048 --iters 150 --rand_prefixes
done
```

Mateo R.: dmesg/kernel excerpts: 
```
[2141597515.45] nvidia: page fault storm, initiating migration
[2141597516.88] kernel: ttm: alloc failed, fallback triggered
[2141597517.12] kernel: GPU OOM: task model_runner(45902) killed
```

Lin S.: quick hypothesis list for RCA (to be expanded):
- H1: KV cache growth + grouped/batched client traffic produced transient working set exceeding GPU RAM -> paging + OOMs.
- H2: allocator fragmentation (small free segments) prevented satisfying large contiguous allocations even though aggregate free memory existed.
- H3: sudden burst from grouped-batching exposed allocator rounding/pathological slab sizes -> fragmentation hotspot.
- H4: a single host had a high-watermark leftover from earlier large requests (carryover), causing it to fail first and domino other hosts due to reroutes.

Lin S.: owners & next actions:
- Aya N.: run repro and upload perf profiles & heap histograms -> due 2141598000
- Mateo R.: collect full `nvidia-smi -q` series + driver logs + allocator debug -> uploaded to gs://redwood-incident-logs/2141597530/nvidia_full.log (done)
- Priya K.: finalize customer comms and gather replay requests -> ongoing
- Jordan H.: coordinate temporary cluster-wide limit if we see recurrence -> standing by
- Lin S.: write RCA draft, correlate P50/P95 deltas and error windows, and propose mitigations -> ETA EOD

Priya K.: recording customer impact numbers for RCA: preliminary P50 baseline ~110ms -> incident peak ~760ms; P95 observed ~2.1s; errors peaked ~20% for about 8m; customer-visible 504 window ~10m. will include precise numbers from metrics.

Aya N.: early repro notes: with B>=10 and seq 2k we see sustained allocator churn and fragmentation metrics rise; trying to capture `cudaMallocRetry` counters and allocator free list snapshots.

Lin S.: immediate short-term mitigations agreed: keep max_batch=5 cluster-wide for model-runner-99, keep kvcache disabled on runner-99b while we investigate, and spin an extra replica if needed to relieve load.

Jordan H.: handoff: passing to Lin S. for RCA and post-incident actions. Lin will own the timeline, hypothesis tracking, and writing the formal RCA doc. @lin please include replay assistance notes for Priya.

Lin S.: taking it. planned follow-ups: deep allocator dive with eng-ml, evaluate kvcache eviction caps, test server-side batch-shaping, and consider allocator defrag/compaction patches. scheduling a working session for tomorrow with runtime, eng-ml, and allocator engineers.

Priya K.: confirmed two tenant replay requests logged; saved IDs in ticket and bucket for ops to help.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (max_batch throttled, kvcache selectively disabled), status=stabilizing. Next update will be the RCA thread.

Lin S.: final note: will attach timeline, logs, reproduction artifacts, and proposed long-term mitigations to the RCA doc. last_message_ts=2141597899
